items.headline: S&P upgrades Sri Lanka to 'B-'
items.summary: S&P Global Ratings lifted Sri Lanka's long-term sovereign rating from CCC+ to B- with a stable outlook, citing strong revenue growth, rising reserves and resilient growth. It flagged energy risks linked to the Middle East war, a possible El Niño and an interest bill near 40% of revenue.

items.headline: GMOA backs November 30 islandwide strike
items.summary: The Government Medical Officers' Association will support the one-day strike called by teachers' and principals' unions, who say the 2027 Budget ignores their grievances. It has not said how doctors will take part.

items.headline: Amber thunderstorm warning for 14 districts
items.summary: The Met Department warned of severe lightning, rain above 100 mm in places and winds of 60–70 kmph until 11:30 PM tonight, covering all of Colombo, Gampaha, Kalutara, Galle, Matara, Ratnapura and Kegalle plus parts of seven other districts. Flash floods, landslides and power cuts are possible.

items.headline: Constable who supplied T-56 rifle deported from Dubai
items.summary: A former Mount Lavinia police constable accused of handing his service T-56 rifle to organised criminals, and of running drug networks in Anuradhapura, was deported from Dubai and arrested by the CID at the airport.

items.headline: Gotabaya testifies in Lalith-Kugan case
items.summary: Former President Gotabaya Rajapaksa gave evidence online for about an hour in the 2011 disappearance case of activists Lalith Kumar Weeraraj and Kugan Muruganandhan. The Jaffna Magistrate's Court will record further evidence on February 12.

items.headline: No ban on phones in police stations
items.summary: Public Security Minister Ananda Wijepala told Parliament there is no circular stopping the public from carrying phones into police stations, though limits may apply to suspects in cells.

items.headline: Rs. 950 million for demining in 2027
items.summary: The government has set aside Rs. 950 million for next year's landmine clearance, and Foreign Minister Vijitha Herath briefed diplomats from 19 countries and UN agencies on the programme.

items.headline: Police explain Jaffna restaurant demolition
items.summary: Police said the part of the 'Matara Ambula' restaurant pulled down in Jaffna was an illegal structure on RDA land, removed under a July court order, and that viral social media posts distorted the facts.

items.headline: School year ends December 4
items.summary: An Education Ministry circular says government and approved private schools close on December 4, and the new school year begins on January 4, 2027.

items.headline: East Terminal to hit 50% capacity this month
items.summary: Deputy Minister Janitha Ruwan Kodithuwakku said Colombo Port's East Terminal should reach half capacity this month, with one automated yard lane running and 10 more being activated.

items.headline: Tea export earnings down 6% in October
items.summary: October tea exports earned about US$118.8 million, down from US$126.5 million a year earlier, as volumes fell. Ten-month earnings are down nearly 7%, though shipments to Türkiye more than doubled.

items.headline: ADB warns Sri Lanka may lose export ground
items.summary: The ADB said rivals winning preferential trade deals, such as India's EU negotiations, could squeeze Sri Lankan exporters, and urged reforms to cut trade costs and attract investment.

items.headline: IRD offices open this weekend
items.summary: Inland Revenue regional offices will open on November 28 and 29 to issue PINs and TINs ahead of the November 30 income tax return deadline.

items.headline: 16 hurt in Ratnapura bus-truck crash
items.summary: A bus heading to Ratnapura collided with a tipper truck on the Ratnapura–Avissawella road this morning, injuring 16 people, five of them seriously.

items.headline: HIV cases rising among young people
items.summary: Health data show a steady rise in HIV infections among 15–24-year-olds since 2010, with 874 new cases detected in 2025. Testing and treatment are free at government clinics.

items.headline: CERT warns of website supply-chain attack
items.summary: Sri Lanka CERT urged organisations to check their sites after a global attack that injected malicious JavaScript into third-party scripts and hit 178 organisations.

items.headline: Kingswood captain takes hat-trick, 11 wickets
items.summary: Kenula Pihilianga took a hat-trick and 11 wickets as Kingswood College beat Christ King College by an innings and 117 runs in Under-19 Division II cricket.
